items.summary: World of Warcraft : Forever is riding high thanks to its popular beta and upcoming launch, but retail WoW's Mi

content.v: World of Warcraft : Forever is riding high thanks to its popular beta and upcoming launch, but retail WoW's Midnight expansion feels like it's in a state of crisis by comparison.

The two different versions of WoW couldn't be in more different places. Forever seems to be extremely popular, with Blizzard developers commenting how its beta is breaking records . Blizzard itself has also been more communicative regarding Forever than ever before, with weekly podcasts diving into community topics, forum posts addressing various issues, and frequent updates addressing balance problems and bugs.

Midnight seems to be in the opposite corner. Its latest content update, patch 12.1.5, went live October 13. In addition to new story quests that continue the expansion's main narrative, it added a new single-boss raid and a long-teased mega delve (officially called a labyrinth) that gives solo-focused players an almost raid-like experience.

Unfortunately, the patch was released in a bug-riddled state. The Kindo'jan labyrinth, arguably the patch's biggest feature, saw players running into issue after issue. Some players complained about not earning credit for boss kills and being unable to collect rewards. One particularly nasty bug had players falling through the floor of the labyrinth's final boss arena, making it so the labyrinth couldn't be completed. Other players cited issues with delve companion Valeera dying too quickly or failing to do proper boss mechanics.

Many of the most glaring bugs (like falling through the floor) were fixed in a hotfix deployed on October 16, but labyrinths still have a major issue: no save points . When Blizzard first detailed labyrinths, it implied players would be able to start one, make some progress, and come back to finish it at a later time. Blizzard's exact wording was that players would be able to "venture through them in a single epic session or tackle them piece by piece over time, progressing at your own pace."

That currently isn't true, as the labyrinth has no checkpoints and must be completed in a single session. Labyrinths taking at least an hour or so to complete, combined with various bugs preventing progress and no way to save and come back to them later, is making for an incredibly frustrating experience. It's unclear if the lack of checkpoints is a bug, an unannounced change on Blizzard's part, or just some kind of oversight, but it's not a great debut for Midnight's newest feature.
Story spoilers for WoW: Midnight patch 12.1.5 below.

Bugs and issues surrounding labyrinths are just one part of why patch 12.1.5 has proven unpopular. The patch is also catching flak for its story, specifically how it killed off a major character unceremoniously. Liadrin, a blood elf paladin and one of the main characters players have interacted with over the course of Midnight, dies facing off against Kithix, the resurrected Old God general that serves at the patch's new raid encounter.

However, she doesn't die in any kind of epic or heroic way. Instead, judging from the post-raid cinematic, she dies from what seems to be exhaustion, having wielded the power of the light too strongly in the battle against Kithix. After Kithix's defeat, Liadrin utters "Darkness will never prevail" before crumpling to the ground and dying.

WoW is not a stranger to having major characters die. It famously happened with Varyian Wrynn, the leader of the Alliance, during the start of the game's Legion expansion. But unlike Varyian's epic death, Liadrin's feels anticlimactic. The fact that it occurs during a .5 patch that feels disconnected to the game's larger narrative makes the story beat feel unnecessary.

Adding salt to the wound is that her death looks to be in service of a recurring and unpopular trend in recent WoW storylines where old rivalries and feuds between factions are easily reconciled. In Liadrin's case, her death brings together the blood elves and the Amani trolls, though Blizzard does make a point in a post-raid quest to emphasise the two groups are not allies despite now being at peace. Blizzard may have said its putting the "war" back in Warcraft during BlizzCon 2026, but all of its recent story beats have seen ancient enemies coming together and cooperating, and Liadrin's death only serves to reinforce that.

This isn't the first time a .5 patch has been met with negative reception from WoW's players. It was only back in April that Blizzard released patch 12.0.5 in an extremely buggy state . Player outcry saw Blizzard go as far to issue a public apology , stating it was "taking lessons learned from this launch to help ensure this doesn't happen again," and that "we will do better." Flash forward six months later, and it doesn't seem like much has changed.

That puts Midnight in a weird place overall. Blizzard barely talked about modern WoW at this year's BlizzCon. It teased Midnight's final content patch that will see players finally confront Xal'atath once and for all, but didn't share more details about what to expect from the game's next expansion, The Last Titan, despite it being slated to release next year.

Instead, Blizzard put almost all its emphasis on WoW: Forever, a new, WoW Classic-inspired version of Blizzard's MMORPG that adds new content and visual upgrades to the old-school version of Azeroth. In an interview with GameSpot, Blizzard shared more details on what to expect from WoW: Forever's future and its endgame. WoW: Forever launches November 4.

items.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases this week, and with gaming consoles and capable PC rigs now more expen

content.v: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases this week, and with gaming consoles and capable PC rigs now more expensive than ever, you might be wondering if there is another way to play.
Thankfully, there is, but there are a few things you need to know before jumping in.
How to play MW4 without a console or PC
With Game Pass:
Modern Warfare 4 is not included with Xbox Game Pass this year, but if you're a subscriber you can leverage the "stream your own game" program to play it that way, after purchasing it outright.
This isn't locked away to any specific tier of Game Pass, either. You can subscribe to Game Pass Essential, Premium, or Ultimate to stream MW4.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/COD1_98947f.jpg?w=636
With GeForce Now:

Nvidia's streaming service, GeForce Now, will be another way to play Modern Warfare 4 without any expensive hardware like a new console or high-end PC. Or at least we think so. Nvidia hasn't outright confirmed this, but people are playing the campaign early access via GeForce Now , so it stands to reason that it will be officially supported at launch for everyone.
After buying the game outright, you'll be able to stream MW4 on GeForce Now by subscribing to one of the platform's membership tiers.

GeForce Now has multiple tiers, including a free ad-supported membership. There are also $10/month and $20/month tiers with no ads and higher-fidelity experiences. There are also day passes available.
For more, check out the GeForce Now website .
Pros and cons of streaming

Before subscribing to Game Pass or GeForce Now, people should know that playing a twitch shooter like Modern Warfare 4 over the internet might not always be the perfect experience. After all, a cloud service works best with a strong and stable connection, and that's not always a guarantee. However, many people report good experiences, and as always, your mileage may vary.
Something else to consider is that, starting in November, Microsoft will implement caps on how many hours people can stream via Game Pass before they must pay more to keep playing.

The benefits of streaming are pretty obvious: You don't need any expensive hardware. This is because a game is streamed on high-end hardware and beamed to your screen, whatever that may be. You will still need a controller or a keyboard and mouse setup, but you might have those things already, and if you don't, they cost significantly less than a new console or a powerful PC.
Why are consoles and PCs so expensive today?

The Xbox Series X|S and PS5 consoles were released in 2020, but today, six years later, they are more expensive than ever. Historically, console prices come down instead of going up. So what's driving the price increases? The AI-fueled demand for components and memory is to blame, as is the war in Iran that's driving up oil prices. There are numerous other macroeconomic factors at play, too, including tariffs.

Companies like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo want to keep making money in this environment. Instead of eating the costs (while they make huge profits and collect tariff refunds), they are charging people more to maintain their margins.

The Switch 2 is among the cheapest ways to play MW4 this year, with that console starting at $500 (up from $450 at launch). The PS5 now starts at $600 (up from $400 at launch) and the latest Xbox consoles are more expensive, too. The Series S now goes for $500 (was $300) and Series X for $750 ($500 at launch). In short, you're in for major sticker shock if you're buying a new console.
For PC players, it's more expensive than ever to build a capable rig, but your price will vary depending on the setup you want, preconfigured or made yourself.
For more, check out GameSpot's Modern Warfare 4 campaign review , and keep checking back for more coverage on DMZ and multiplayer when the game goes live on October 23.

items.summary: Hundreds of PSA-graded trading cards worth more than $100,000 were reportedly stolen from a FedEx truck over t

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/19/hundreds-of-psa-graded-trading-cards-stolen-from-fedex-truck-1792435194146.jpg
Hundreds of PSA-graded trading cards worth more than $100,000 were reportedly stolen from a FedEx truck over the weekend, leaving collectors distraught — and the damage is still being calculated.

On October 17, a collector named SKY-B posted on Twitter/X claiming that PSA had notified him via email that a FedEx truck carrying his 104-card collection had been burglarized after leaving its Southern California location. According to SKY-B, more than $100,000 worth of cards had been taken.

In its email, which SKY-B shared in a reply , PSA outlined steps it had taken to rectify the situation as best as possible, saying it had deactivated certificates for the affected items, notified its commerce partners of the stolen cards, and is actively working with both FedEx and law enforcement to investigate the theft.

"We will compensate you for the items from your order that were involved, which is based on fair market value up to the Maximum Insured Value ("MIV") you selected for each item." @natsturner, I pray you handle this and take care of everyone affected in the most professional manner possible. I have an awful feeling PSA is going to be extremely unfair on what the values of these cards are.

PSA also stated that it would compensate SKY-B for the items in his collection, the monetary amount for which is “based on fair market value up to the Maximum Insured Value" he selected for each item.

In a YouTube video , SKY-B explained that the stolen order had taken him more than two years to accumulate, which included “many irreplaceable cards” that he fears he’ll never see again. He said that he hand-delivered the cards to PSA to be graded at the National Card Show in July, and three months later, his extensive collection could be lining the pockets of the thieves who stole it.

SKY-B says he spent $8,000 to have the cards graded, which had a maximum insurance value of $156,000 each. The collector claimed that several of the cards in his collection exceeded this maximum value, but says that he wasn’t “upcharged” by PSA because of this — making him worry that the company will “destroy” him with “low-ball values” of all his cards.

“Honestly, that’s what hurts the most, outside of obviously being absolutely financially destroyed here,” he said, referring to likely never seeing his carefully-curated collection again. “...I am currently out all of the money that it cost to acquire these cards, I’m out all the PSA grading fees, and I don’t have and I probably will never see any of these cards in person.”

SKY-B wasn’t the only one impacted by the FedEx truck theft; content creator and fellow collector Boston Card Hunter claimed that he was approached by a “major PSA dealer” who told him that customers had lost an estimated “$500K of declared value.”

After speaking with other affected dealers and collectors, Boston Card Hunter stated that FedEx trucks have now become targets for thieves, and speculated that dealers might handle their own shipping and handling from PSA moving forward.

Currently, Boston Card Hunter has compiled a list of 383 serialized cards that were allegedly stolen from this FedEx truck, which include a 1995 Upper Deck 23K Gold Michael Jordan 50,000 Print Run, a 2024 One Piece Simplified Chinese 1st Anniversary Set Nami, and many other cards from various anime series, trading card games, and sports figures.
Over on Reddit , other card collectors claimed to have also been victims of the FedEx theft, with one saying their PSA 9 Smaug the Magnificent card from Magic: The Gathering had been burgled.

In a statement to IGN, PSA reiterated the steps it has taken to help law enforcement and FedEx recover the items and investigate the theft, as well as contacting customers to compensate them based on fair market value.
PSA's full statement is as follows:
"We are aware of a theft involving a third-party shipping vehicle carrying PSA-graded items. We are working closely with law enforcement and the carrier as the investigation continues.

"We have deactivated the certificates for the stolen items and notified marketplace partners so they can be on the lookout for rare and serialized items. Our customer service team has contacted affected customers directly and is arranging compensation based on fair market value.

"We understand the impact this has on collectors involved, many of whom see these cards as far more than a financial asset. Our team is focused on supporting them. We take this incident seriously, and we will continue working with law enforcement to hold those responsible accountable."

This is the latest development to go viral within the card collecting community after Pokemon TCG collectors were put on blast for offering to trade their purebred puppies in exchange for cards at two separate card shows.
Image Credits: Marcin Golba/NurPhoto via Getty Images

items.summary: British actor Rahul Kohli (Saros, Midnight Mass) has a pitch for a new L.A. Noire game, and it sounds pretty g

content.v: British actor Rahul Kohli (Saros, Midnight Mass) has a pitch for a new L.A. Noire game, and it sounds pretty great. Speaking to BAFTA Games , Kohli said he would like to see the franchise return with a spinoff that takes players through different time periods, as a cop, as they investigate different crimes.

One such setting could be Victorian England, with a storyline focused on hunting down Jack the Ripper, Kohli said. Another could take players to the '80s in California as they pursue the Night Stalker, the actor added.
"We could jump around and be a cop in different times. I would be down for that," Kohli said. "I loved it. I adored L.A. Noire."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/LANoire_ece858.jpg?w=636

In particular, Kohli said he was a big fan of developer Team Bondi's facial-capture system which created lifelike expressions in the game, down to granular details like how a person’s eyebrows might move.

In a game where players had to read people's facial expressions, this was a big deal, and one can only imagine how much further the technology could go today. However, Kohli said he wants a new L.A. Noire game with the same tech and the same engine.
"I want that. I don't want an improvement to it. That was part of the charm," he said.
L.A. Noire was released in 2011. It never got a sequel, and its developer, Team Bondi, later disbanded. A virtual reality game, L.A. Noire: The VR Case Files, was released in 2017.
Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick said the company was looking at future projects in all of its franchises , and that includes L.A. Noire.

Back in 2012, Rockstar said a sequel to L.A. Noire was a “possibility.” At the time, the developer said, “We don’t always rush to make sequels, but that does not mean we won’t get to them eventually. We have so many games we want to make, and the issue is always one of bandwidth and timing.”
Recently, a rumor emerged that a new L.A. Noire game is now in the works, and it will have players collecting clues to try to find the Zodiac Killer .

items.summary: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 has cast Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima in a role that will see him reprise hi

others.title: 小岛秀夫重返赛博朋克宇宙《Edgerunners》第二季

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/19/hideo-kojima-cyberpunk-edgerunners-2-1792430384764.png
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 has cast Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima in a role that will see him reprise his part from Cyberpunk 2077 .

Series game developer CD Projekt Red confirmed the news in a social media post on X/Twitter . The message teased that it's more than a throwaway part, too, as Kojima will be seen playing "the famous braindance director who was at Konpeki Plaza in Cyberpunk 2077" (via X's machine translation).

The real-life game director was quick to respond and share his excitement, as well as a few pictures from his time recording his lines. His full statement, minus a few fun emojis, is as follows: "I make a cameo appearance in the anime series Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 as Hideyoshi Oshima, the character who appeared in the previous game."
I make a cameo appearance in the anime series “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” as Hideyoshi Oshima, the character who appeared in the previous game. 🙏🙇🏻😅🫶👍 https://t.co/OuUaazFfR4

Cyberpunk 2077 players were treated to an unexpected visit from the Kojima Productions lead when they first traveled to Night City back in 2020. It's a moment that wasn't actually directly tied to V's mainline quest and surprisingly easy to miss, but yes, if players search Arasaka's Konpeki Plaza hard enough, they can find Kojima sitting near a bar.

If you're familiar with Kojima's work on games like Metal Gear Solid and Death Stranding, what he had to say in the Cyberpunk world wasn't too surprising. He enjoyed chatting about the in-universe memory-exploring mechanic, braindances, as he wanted his "productions to convey real, raw human emotion." When stopped by V, he asks the player if they have any pitches to show him.

"The feeling when you combine happiness and melancholy, or being calm with an underlying sense of anxiety," he says in the game. "These complex, realistic feelings and emotions are what I aspire to recreate... woven into much better stories, of course."

Kojima's Oshima will now bring his love for braindance technology to Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 when it premieres tomorrow, October 20, 2026. All 10 episodes of the second season will drop at the same time. IGN called this second anime trip into Night City "Amazing" in our 9/10 review .
"Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 delivers the gory, action-packed goods, even if it doesn’t quite hit the highs of its predecessor,” we said.

Kojima is hard at work on games like Physint and OD , but that doesn't mean he hasn't had time for one or even a few cameos. We know now that Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 was one of the few anime projects he teased earlier this month, but we're still waiting to see the "big movie" he filmed .

Returning to Cyberpunk 2077 or playing it for the first time? We’ve got a new and improved Cyberpunk interactive map to help you find every mission, Iconic item, and collectible in the game. Plus, we’ve also got a full walkthrough for the base game, a Phantom Liberty walkthrough , and an overview of all the Cyberpunk 2077 endings so you don’t make a choice you regret. And we can’t ignore the various romance options you can smooch, which also impact how V’s story concludes.

items.title: 一级方程式赛车有一个很大的人工智能问题。下一场 F1 比赛应该重现它吗？
items.summary: Formula One's 2026 regulation changes have introduced AI into motorsport, taking control away from drivers. Sh

content.v: Since it acquired the F1 license in 2009, UK-based studio Codemasters has walked a precarious sim-cade tightrope with its F1 games. It’s never been as rigorous in its physics simulation as iRacing, rFactor or Assetto Corsa Competizione, but neither has it shied away from capturing the details and demands of the sport and packaging them up into an entertaining and ultimately rewarding race weekend.

But replicating those details will introduce a difficult new element when it comes to the next F1 game. Machine learning AI supercomputers are taking control away from Formula One drivers. Borne of the new 2026 season regulation changes, it’s a phenomenon that’s usually subtle because it works by controlling the power deployment of extremely complex hybrid power units. That’s quite tricky to eyeball from the onboard broadcast cameras. But when that AI-controlled power deployment goes wrong, it makes itself extremely conspicuous.

At a drenched Sepang circuit on the first weekend of October, race fans were treated to the sight of 22 vehicles representing the pinnacle of motorsport losing throttle and trundling at 20mph on the warmup lap. It was the result of a software glitch triggered by the wet weather and the way Sepang’s sectors are configured, and it required all teams to install a software update to their cars before the race could begin.

Lewis Hamilton, whose Ferrari came to a complete standstill on the start-finish straight, later reported that he had to do a full engine restart, essentially CTRL+ALT+DEL’ing his vehicle on the track in order to gain back some throttle control and power deployment.
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/19/f1-25-1792417655042.jpg

One race earlier at Baku, Valtteri Bottas retired in the later stages of the race after suffering a very unusual accident. It looked as though the veteran Finn had completely missed his brake marker going into turn 15, locking up and crashing into the barriers. Only afterwards did Bottas reveal that the crash wasn’t down to driver error, but the energy deployment system.

“It was quite strange,” he told GPBlog . “On the same lap I went off in turn one, I went wide. Then I think the system’s got a bit confused. I had a huge super-clip, and then when I hit the brakes only the front brakes would work, almost like I wasn’t harvesting anymore with the rears.”

Super-clipping is another bit of autonomous driving whereby the power unit reduces throttle in order to harvest energy for the electric motor. It’s a bizarre sight and sound – a Formula One car coasting into a corner way before the braking zone, as though it’s running out of fuel.

What these incidents reveal is just how much of the 2026 F1 car is out of its driver’s control. And oddly enough it isn’t so much these obvious moments of malfunction that are the problem, it’s when things are operating as planned. That scenario’s just as damaging to the sport.

After pulling off an overtake on seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton in Suzuka earlier in the season, Lando Norris later told the official McLaren website “the battery deployment triggered, even though I didn’t really want it to, and I had to overtake Lewis as a result.
“That meant I was then a sitting duck on the next straight, where I had actually wanted to use the battery… For me, that’s taking too much control away from the driver.”

The fact that Norris could accidentally overtake 106-time race winner Lewis Hamilton, and himself feel hopeless to defend his position moments later, tells you all you need to know about how powerful the electric energy deployment is in the 2026 F1 cars, which feature about a 50:50 ratio of turbo engine and electric motor power.

It also explains why many have criticised the racing as so unnatural to watch: the power difference between a car deploying that electric power in ‘boost’ mode and a car without boost is enormous, so much so that it looks like cars from different categories racing on the same track. Or, as Charles Leclerc put it earlier this season, “ This is like the mushroom in Mario Kart .”
So you’ve got drivers openly criticising the current regulations, power units glitching out and requiring software updates before the race can go ahead, and people accidentally overtaking each other.
Now imagine you’re a developer at Codemasters watching this unfold. What do you do?

Codemasters has always put emphasis on the sport’s very specific details. Over the years, that’s meant you’ve always had to pay attention to tire wear and engine map modes, for example. In the recent games’ driver career mode, your power units become worn and using more than the allocated number over the course of a season incurs a grid penalty. You participate in Friday practice sessions to build up currency that can be used to research and manufacture new engine and aero parts.

When DRS was introduced in 2011, Codemasters also introduced it to F1 2011. Likewise ERS battery management in 2014. It’s always taken pride in simulating the minutiae of the sport, as it appears on TV screens that season, even if the simulation itself isn’t as mathematically forensic as a hardcore racing sim.

The 2026 season DLC goes some way towards capturing the current regulations. Battery deployment is an important part of racing, and there’s some nuance to how and when you harvest battery, depending on whether you’re in a straight zone, and whether your throttle is pinned above 90%. Crucially though, the game keeps you largely in control of battery harvesting and deployment unless you enable a driving aid to let the game handle it. That’s very different to the AI auto-deployment situation with its multitudinous bugs we’re seeing on the real track.

So how should F1 27 capture this energy deployment situation? It’s hard to imagine how this auto-deployment of electric power will add to your sense of satisfaction in either solo or online play, let alone how the differences between teams and their AI supercomputers might affect race outcomes. This puts the next F1 game in a fascinating position. The better a job it does of simulating Formula One, the more it will feel buggy and broken. If F1 27 goes for maximum realism, cars will slow down on straights when you’re got the throttle pinned. You’ll experience random surges in your car’s pace, and then be left feeling like you’re in a GP3 car a couple of corners later. Maybe your team-mate will trounce you because their AI deployment’s simply working better than yours.

Fans have always wanted F1 games to offer racing that’s as close to the real thing as possible until now. F1 27 might be the first time they’re genuinely ok with a developer using some creative licensing.

Best case scenario, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) bails Codemasters out from having to make that call. Planned regulation changes for the 2027 season will allow the cars’ electric power harvesting to pick up more battery during braking zones, while deploying less on straights. So the boost button should feel less like a Mario Kart mushroom, and we should see less super-clipping on straights. Should .

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

Saint Moses the Black, who converted from a life of crime to one of ascetic anchoritism, once told his brothers that if they had aught to learn they need only sit in their cells: "Your cell will teach you everything." I am following his example. I am trading in my life of crime for one of contemplation. I am returning to my cell.
What I mean is, Los Santos Customs has to briefly go on hiatus but will return in the near future. Anyway, today I was an Uber driver with a gun.

I installed Goober & Goober Eats – Realistic Rideshare & Food Delivery , which introduces the gig economy to the hot streets of Los Santos. The premise is simple: you're an Uber guy now. You can bring up your phone (not the regular phone you use in regular GTA 5, but an entirely new, work phone that the mod summons into being and binds to a different key). Then you mark your labour as commoditisable and off you go.

It's all quite well-ordered. A helpful line on your map guides you to your pickup, then a second takes you to your client. Of course, as we all know, I can only obtain a car by teleporting into the nearest one, which was a minor issue, but for the most part I had no problems picking up my order.

Delivering it was another matter. My destination was in San Andreas' far north, easily a couple minutes' drive away (and that's if you manage to not get shot to death, caught in a gang war, or flattened by a passing flying truck). I teleport every 50 seconds to random places on the map.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/dcBbrExrmuAaqLgWrR5YWE-1920-80.gif

I gave it the old college try, though, putting pedal to the metal in an attempt to deliver a burrito at physics-defying speed. It was only when I was teleported into immovability between two pylons in a cable car station that I decided it simply wasn't gonna happen. My paralysis did at least give me time to appreciate my notifications, which told me "The Nihilist Sailors have entered Los Santos". Indeed.

I quickly manually teleported to my destination and dropped off the order. I made like $100 or something. Then, just as quickly, I was whisked to the airport, where a group of furries shot my bodyguard to death.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ZF5ZJsyvbhJRVSDmd9H3jA-1920-80.jpg

items.title: 萨罗斯通过 Zenith 更新获得 Boss Rush 和大量难度选项
items.summary: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026. If you've been wait

content.v: Saros is a phenomenal sci-fi shooter, and it currently stands as my favorite game of 2026. If you've been waiting for the right time to play it--or to play it again--then developer Housemarque has some good news. The new Zenith update is now available for free, adding a boss rush and difficulty options that should appeal to both newcomers and seasoned veterans.

First up, the boss rush. Dubbed "Overlord Rush," the mode comes with its own dedicated leaderboards and tasks you with taking out a series of the game's bosses. Rather than starting on the first boss and fighting uninterrupted to the very end, they're divided into separate "sets" that each contain three fights. Overlord Rush is available via the Primary robot in the main hub area.

The new settings and difficulty modifiers, meanwhile, allow you to both reduce and increase the game's challenge, customizing it to fit your preferences. The "Slow Game Speed" setting lets you slow down the entire game so you have more time to react to projectiles, and you can tweak exactly how much it slows down and even if you want it to turn on automatically when combat starts. An "Auto-fire" setting also eliminates the need to actually pull the trigger when you aim, which can be handy when you're primarily focused on dodging incoming attacks. You can think of it almost like a Vampire Survivors-style tool.

Carcosan Modifiers were already in the game at launch, giving you the choice to make the game easier or harder--or a mix of both in different parts of the game--but a whole bunch more were added with Zenith. New Protection modifiers include a "Corruption Melee Enhancement," as outlined on the PlayStation Blog , which gives your melee attacks more power if you acquire Corruption, which is typically not a good thing to have.
Trial Modifiers, meanwhile, make the game more challenging, and when combined with the new ultra-hard endgame Eclipse Layers, you'll be able to put all your skills to the test.
Saros is available exclusively on PS5. In our Saros review , Richard Wakeling called it an "incredible game that does more than just refine what worked before."

items.title: 《星球大战：银河赛车手》中的比迪·布拉斯由邪恶马戏团马戏团领班职业摔跤手配音，这是有道理的
items.summary: Star Wars has had no shortage of breakout alien stars over the decades--from Chewbacca in the original trilogy

content.v: Star Wars has had no shortage of breakout alien stars over the decades--from Chewbacca in the original trilogy to Grogu from The Mandalorian--but in Star Wars: Galactic Racer, that honor belongs to Biddy Blas. Who is Biddy Blas? A hotshot racer in the game, with an ego the size of a Death Star and a voice that sounds like a TIE Fighter fueled by nightmares— that's who Biddy Blas is. And in real life, the man behind the voice is none other than indie UK wrestler and actor Richard Summers-Calvert, who is down to "scrib doon" some autographs from fans.

Performing under the name "The Spectacular Tw*t" Charles Crowley, Summers-Calvert has popped up in multiple pro wrestling promotions, including a recent appearance in Ring of Honor. The actor and wrestler says he's been humbled by Biddy Blas's popularity since he was introduced in Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

"I could tell Biddy Blas was gonna be popular early on," Summers-Calvert said to Soundsphere . "Then I woke up the next day and he'd blown up a bit, and then the next day it kind of dawned on me that this isn’t normal."

Since then, Summers-Calvert says he has received a ton of messages, mentions, and even "Biddy Blas thirst traps" online. For the role, Summers-Calvert recalled that the audition called for a small man who was constantly on the edge and overcompensating, which convinced the pro wrestler to raise his pitch. The game directors liked it, but the role wasn't easy--especially when he had to perform his lines in the Star Wars language of Huttese. "I keep seeing online people talking about like cuteness aggression, and they love him so much they want to throw him at the wall," Summers-Calvert added.
The popularity of Biddy Blas has only grown in recent weeks, as the character has been referenced in numerous memes and even by sports teams, like the Pittsburgh Steelers:

For pro wrestling fans, it's another example of how the theatrical side of sports entertainment has naturally connected with video games. Roman Reigns, who plays Akuma in the new Street Fighter movie, recently commented on the power of video games and how performers prefer to spend their downtime between shows with a console. Other wrestlers like Kenny Omega have also incorporated video games into their movesets and personas, referencing their favorite titles as signature attacks in the ring. At this rate, don't be too surprised if a Wrestler starts hitting his opponents with the "Scrib Doon" finisher.

If you haven't checked it out yet, Star Wars: Galactic Racer is now available for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. It's pretty great, blending Burnout- and Wipeout-inspired speed with a well-designed roguelite core that makes every race feel challenging and dangerous.

items.title: 您可以在 6 小时内以不到 12 美元的价格制作这款 DIY 控制器，但您愿意吗？
items.summary: I think I'll stick with my GameSir Nova Lite.

content.v: In my past life as a console gamer, I was wary of any controller not bundled in with my first-party hardware. These days though, there are lots of excellent PC gamepad options—particularly in the budget category—but how cheap is too cheap?

Our current pick for the best PC controller that won't hurt your wallet is the GameSir Nova Lite . This costs comfortably under $30 on a good day, but how low can you go in the budget realm? Well, how about a pad you can make yourself in about six hours for €10 (or about $11.22)? The catch is… uh, well, just look at it .

Dubbed the Undercooked V0.4, this thing doesn't have a D-pad or even a full set of face buttons. Instead, this project limits itself to a single analogue stick, 'X' and 'A' inputs, a menu button, and a 'B' button that's been relegated to the pad's right shoulder.

According to the creator, Lazy_Duck, "the idea was to make it simple, affordable and that you could get all components even in the smallest electronics shop quick and cheap." As such, this simplified pad doesn't even feature a full PCB.

Instead, you'll need a protoboard with an RP2040-Zero microcontroller—that is, if you fancy DIY-ing something that looks a bit like the tech you would have seen coming out of East Germany after the wall came down. With only four buttons and a stick, it definitely gets points for novelty at the very least.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CJAftkCrSyitfLrARKE2RK-1920-80.jpg

The body may also earn itself a few more points for durability. Made from 150 g of 3D printed filament, the shell is then stuck together with heat-set threaded inserts. Basically, this gamepad should be able to take a tumble, or indeed being flung across the room.

All of those 3D printed ridges don't look like they'll be especially comfortable in the hands over extended periods, so you may want to sand the outer parts of the shell before putting it all together. Mind you, sanding may not do much for comfort given the back side of this controller is completely flat.
My fingers are aching just looking at it. Still, if you're looking for a cheap and cheerful electronics project, you can't go too wrong with this, even if you don't end up actually using it.
